newsitem.title: JORDAN: Jordan shares depressed at start of week.
newsitem.headline: Jordan shares depressed at start of week.

text.p: Jordanian stocks fell 0.82 percent at the start of weekly trading on Saturday in subdued activity as investors avoided the bourse because of concerns over the regional peace process and business deals in Iraq.
"There was hardly any activity in the market, with only some limited institutional buying on a few stock," said Husam al-Hanbali, broker at Jordan Arab Banking Corporation's brokerage arm.
The official Amman Financial Market (AFM) index shed 1.27 points to 153.75 points, its lowest level since early January, in low turnover of 563,013 dinars ($795,216).
Arab Bank, which dropped 3.25 dinars to 256.25 dinars in trade worth 179,450 dinars, alone accounted for a third of Saturday's trading volume.
The downward pressure on the bank bluechip stock, which is heavily weighed in the official 60-share index, helped drag the bourse even lower in depressed trade, brokers said.

Market rumours Arab Bank may not announce in 1997 a widely expected bonus share in its coming AGM because of a delay in approval of a companies law, which eliminates a 15 percent tax on capitalisation through reserves, helped push the stock down.

Renewed uncertainty over the fate of Middle East peace added to investor worries about the fate of $120 million worth of orders won by Jordanian firms under the U.N. "oil-for food" deal, which have yet to be approved by the sanctions committee.
Many industrial firms, especially drug manufacturers, hope Iraq exports will boost performance and use idle capacity.
Some recent buying has been motivated by expectations Iraq orders will produce improved 1997 results.
Growing doubts about the government's seriousness in implementing its privatisation pledge has also kept some investors on the sidelines this week, dealers say.

Only a handful of stock attracted some demand including: Livestock and Poultry which rose 1.75 percent to 0.58 dinars and Jordan Industrial Resources which shed 0.02 dinars to 1.31 dinars in trade worth 31,204 dinars.
The second and third busiest shares, Jordan Cement Factories and Housing Bank, were unchanged at 3.53 dinars and 4.65 dinars respectively.

Arab Potash Company, which recently saw some limited foreign investor interest, shed 0.07 dinars to 6.03 dinars as major institutional and outside buyers who were behind recent market buying were absent, brokers said.
Only five stocks rose against 20 declines on Saturday, while 12 traded but closed unchanged.
The private Pearl Index of the 45 most-traded shares on the exchange shed 0.57 percent to 80.76 points, 3.15 percent down from the start of the year.
